key_insight: PlenopticDreamer synchronizes generative hallucinations across cameras and time so that camera-controlled re-rendered videos remain spatially and temporally consistent in multi-view scenarios.
problem_solved: Addresses the failure of prior camera-conditioned generative re-rendering methods to keep hallucinated regions coherent across multiple viewpoints and over time, reducing flicker, view-inconsistency, and geometry violations in multi-view video.
method: Introduce a plenoptic-aligned generative pipeline that ties hallucinated content to a shared multi-view representation so different cameras see consistent imagery.
Enforce cross-view and temporal synchronization through shared latent codes / cross-view attention and dedicated spatio-temporal consistency losses during training.
Produce camera-conditioned re-renders from the synchronized representation, enabling controllable viewpoint changes while preserving coherent hallucinations.
impact: Makes camera-controlled multi-view video re-rendering practical and reliable for applications like AR/VR, virtual camera navigation, and multi-view editing by greatly reducing hallucination-induced artifacts and instability.
visual_elements: Before/After comparison: same scene re-rendered from multiple views showing inconsistent vs. synchronized hallucinations.
Pipeline diagram: input multi-view frames + camera poses → shared plenoptic representation → synchronized generative module → camera-conditioned re-renders.
Temporal consistency animation/strip: frame sequence highlighting reduced flicker and stable object appearance over time.
Error/consistency heatmap: per-pixel multi-view discrepancy visualized to show improvement quantitatively.
paper_authors: Xiao Fu, Shitao Tang, Min Shi, Xian Liu, Jinwei Gu
